purpose: The aha catalogue. Each pattern is a brief for a retroactive reframing: what the trick is, what the engine must be able to express (capabilities, resolved at run time by compat_check against the real schema and vocabulary), what must be planted early, how it fails, and which deterministic checks guard it. Abstract only: no story.
source_note: Built from the fallback list in the kit brief. The research document's Track 3 was not available to the kit author; if it is attached later, its wording replaces these briefs but compat_check still decides availability.

patterns.name: Innocent Cover-Up
patterns.mechanism: A person conceals an act that is innocent of the crime but shameful or costly to them. The concealment produces the same paper traces guilt would.
presignal: The concealer's unexplained behaviour appears early on routine paper.
The innocent act is established independently by a second record that does not mention the crime.
patterns.failure_mode: The innocent act is too trivial to justify the concealment, or it is announced by a confession.

patterns.name: Background-as-Foreground
patterns.mechanism: The decisive fact sits in a record whose main business is elsewhere: a routine line in a document about something else.
presignal: The host record appears early and is about another matter.
A later record gives the routine line its meaning.
patterns.failure_mode: The line is flagged by phrasing, or it is reachable only by keyword search. Never place it in a world-context record the Desk badges as archive.

patterns.name: Bidirectional Alibi Inversion
patterns.mechanism: An alibi that clears one person, read in the other direction, places them where it matters or removes someone else's cover.
presignal: The alibi is recorded early by a third party, not by the person it clears.
The inverting fact is a time or position recorded independently.
patterns.failure_mode: Times are fuzzy, so the inversion cannot be proved; or the alibi is too convenient to read as innocent.

patterns.name: Negative Clue
patterns.mechanism: The decisive evidence is an absence: an entry that should exist and does not, an action that always happens and did not.
presignal: The normal pattern is established in at least two records before the gap appears.
patterns.failure_mode: The absence is not provably meaningful, or the player reads it as a missing record or a bug.

patterns.name: Department Lens Reversal
patterns.mechanism: A department's assessment, shaped by its bias, misreads its own raw findings. The findings read plainly reverse the assessment.
presignal: The department's bias is visible in at least one earlier, unrelated assessment.
patterns.failure_mode: Assessment language leaks into the findings section, or the bias is invisible so the reversal feels arbitrary.

patterns.name: Identity Collapse
patterns.mechanism: Two apparent people are one person under two references.
presignal: The two references are never present together.
They share one ordinary, checkable attribute recorded in two places.
patterns.failure_mode: Needs a twin-like contrivance or an unprepared disguise.

patterns.name: Identity Fission
patterns.mechanism: One apparent person is two: two holders of one title, badge, initial or account.
presignal: The shared reference is used in two records whose details cannot both belong to one person.
patterns.failure_mode: The split is introduced late instead of being visible in early paper.

patterns.name: Temporal Window Shift
patterns.mechanism: The critical event happened at a different time than the official account says.
presignal: The official time is recorded early.
An independent physical or routine record fixes the true window.
patterns.failure_mode: Clock confusion rather than evidence; too many competing times.

patterns.name: Spatial Relocation
patterns.mechanism: The event happened in a different place than everyone assumes.
presignal: A physical trace of the true place appears early in an unrelated record.
patterns.failure_mode: The geography is unclear, so the relocation cannot be checked.

patterns.name: Motive Polarity Inversion
patterns.mechanism: The apparent motive is the opposite of the real one: an act that looks hostile was protective, or one that looks kind was self-serving.
presignal: The relationship's true temperature is shown early on paper about something else.
patterns.failure_mode: The real motive appears only in a late explanation.

patterns.name: Cross-Modal Sensory Mismatch
patterns.mechanism: Two records of one moment in different modalities disagree: what a log says against what a photograph shows or a transcript hears.
presignal: Both records exist from the start; neither looks suspicious alone.
patterns.failure_mode: The mismatch depends on media the Desk does not render, or on detail only an image could carry.

patterns.name: Fragment Assembly Gestalt
patterns.mechanism: Pieces that are innocuous alone reveal the shape when assembled.
presignal: Each fragment has its own in-world reason to exist.
patterns.failure_mode: Assembly order is ambiguous, or one fragment alone gives the answer.

patterns.name: Unintended Consequence
patterns.mechanism: The harm resulted from an act meant for something else; the person responsible did not intend the outcome.
presignal: The original intention is recorded early as an ordinary request or plan.
patterns.failure_mode: The causal chain has a step no record supports.

patterns.name: Physical Constraint Inversion
patterns.mechanism: A constraint believed to exclude someone actually enables them, or one believed to enable someone excludes them.
presignal: The constraint is stated early as a plain fact of the building, the equipment or the rules.
patterns.failure_mode: The constraint's real behaviour is explained only at the end.

patterns.name: Epistemic Trap
patterns.mechanism: Someone shows knowledge on paper they could only have if they were involved.
presignal: When and how the knowledge became available is fixed by other records.
patterns.failure_mode: A smoking-gun slip. The tell must be quiet and needs a who-knew-what cross-reference.

patterns.name: Symmetrical Alibi Collapse
patterns.mechanism: Two people vouch for each other; one inconsistency collapses both accounts.
presignal: Both accounts are recorded separately and early.
patterns.failure_mode: The collapse needs one person to confess.
